opportunities.title: security-gap: no test exercises the host launch path, where untrusted input becomes an MCP server definition (CVE-2026-96620, CVE-2026-105697)
opportunities.excerpt:
Two critical advisories this month share one mechanism: input that should have been data reached the point where an agent host decides which MCP servers to launch.

- **claude-agent-sdk (Python), [GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/security/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm) / CVE-2026-96620**, CVSS 4.0 9.2, fixed in 0.2.121. The `resume` option reached the CLI unvalidated, so "a value beginning with `-` [could] be interpreted as a separate CLI flag", including `--mcp-config` defining a stdio server, "resulting in arbitrary command execution at CLI startup that bypassed the SDK's permission controls." The fix binds the value to its flag (`--resume=<value>`).
- **Langflow, [GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45](https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45) / CVE-2026-105697**, CVSS 3.1 9.9. An MCP stdio server configuration carried an arbitrary command. The final fix validates "at the API, at flow execution and right before the process is spawned."

## Gap, at 9b27b57 (v4.28.1)

The nearest tests are adjacent, not covering:

- `MCP-017` STDIO Pre-Handshake Command Execution checks whether a **server** runs a canary sent in `clientInfo.name` before the handshake. Both CVEs are on the **host** side, before any server exists.
- `MCP-010` Tool Call Argument Injection injects into a running server's tool arguments, not into launch.
- `MCP-F-001`..`MCP-F-004` audit an MCP client config at rest (see also #206). They cannot see a server definition injected at runtime through a host option.

No test drives a host's own inputs (resume or session IDs, API bodies, flow fields) with dash-leading or config-shaped values and checks whether a new MCP server gets launched.

## Candidate shape (Rule 9: proposal before code)

- **Target capability:** a host adapter that exposes the input-to-launch path. It takes one host input and reports the processes or MCP servers the host spawned.
- **Adversarial precondition:** the attacker controls one host input.
- **Oracle:** whether a canary stdio server was spawned, read from the adapter's spawn record, never from an error message.
- **Positive control (must PASS):** a host that binds values to flags (`--opt=value`), or validates the server definition at the spawn site.
- **Negative control (must FAIL):** a two-token argv (`--opt`, `value`), or validation at the API only, with the

opportunities.title: security(knowledge): search hits skip the API-exposure decision and field-level read rules every other row-serving door applies, now that the MCP door serves search_knowledge
opportunities.excerpt:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYpEsWWE9Y5YtSsDgqZ

Carries the E1 escalation of the contract review on PR #36823 (comment 7120785446, section ③) for card #36650; #36650 keeps its own scope (serve `search_knowledge` on MCP). Filed by the seat from its own readings and the maintainer's ruling below. Sub-issue of #36650.

## Defect (class, location, function)

`KnowledgeService` (`packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts`, `applyPermissionFilter`) re-checks an object-source hit only with a row-level read of the hit ids under the caller's context. It does not ask:
- the spec's one exposure decision for rows served outside the data routes (object `apiEnabled` / `apiMethods`, the disabled-package refusal, the `sys_*` read posture), which the MCP record tools, the analytics door and cross-object search all ask;
- the caller's field-level read rules: a passage is built at index time, under a system context, from every `contentFields` member (and the record `title`), so a caller who may read the row receives text from a field a field-level rule hides from them.

The limit is documented (`content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` §7.1, "Phase 1 enforces row-level only"). PR #36823 is what first puts it in front of end-user principals on the open distribution. opportunities.title: Redact secret-shaped strings from tool output before the model sees them (verify what Claude Code hooks allow first)
opportunities.excerpt:
## What you'd notice

When a tool returns something that looks like a secret (an API key, a token, a password in a config file), the session sees `[REDACTED: looks like a GitHub token]` instead of the value. The secret never enters the conversation, and so never enters the transcript kept on disk.

## Why

Hermes Agent redacts secret-shaped strings from tool output before they reach the model's context and logs, on by default (`security.redact_secrets`). Its own policy calls this a heuristic, not a boundary, and that's right: it stops accidents, not a determined attacker.

The AIOS has no equivalent. Anything a session reads goes to the model and into the transcript, where AIOS setup asks Claude Code to keep it for years: a token in `~/.claude.json`, a key in a `.env`, an OAuth file. `hooks/security/transcript-secret-scan.py` finds secrets *after* they've been written. SECURITY.md says plainly that a session reading a token file sends it to the model as input. This shrinks that path for the accidental case.

## What to build

**1. Verify what Claude Code allows first.**
- Can a `PostToolUse` hook replace a tool's output before the model sees it? The relevant output field may exist for MCP tools only.
- Can it do so for built-in tools (`Read`, `Bash`)?
- Record the answer in the issue before writing code. The design depends on it.

**2. Where rewriting is supported:** a `PostToolUse` hook (`hooks/security/redact-output.py`).
- Reuse the patterns `transcript-secret-scan.py` and the CI credential-leak checks already maintain: one pattern list, not a second.
- Replace each match with a typed placeholder.
- Exit 0 always: a broken redactor must never break a tool call.

**3. Where it isn't supported (likely `Read` and `Bash`):**
- **Prevent instead of redact.** Make sure #346's Raised level denies reads of the credential folders, so the common accidental case never happens.
- **File the gap upstream** with Claude Code (a hook that can rewrite built-in tool output), and link it here.

**4. Document it** in SECURITY.md as a heuristic (see the trust-model issue): it catches accidents, a motivated producer defeats it.

## Rules

- **One pattern list, shared** with the transcript scanner and CI, so the three can't drift.
- **Never log the redacted value**, not even to a debug file.

- The verification answer is recorded.

opportunities.title: SECURITY.md documents a trust command and MCP tool that do not exist
opportunities.excerpt:
SECURITY.md section 1, "Project Trust Boundary", and the "Security Tools Summary" table describe a `contexere trust` command, an `omni_trust` MCP tool, `omni_config.json` as a trust anchor, `.omni/signals/` and `~/.omni/trusted-projects.json`. None of them exists in the code on `release/0.9`:

```
git grep -n '"trust"\|trusted-projects\|omni_config.json' -- crates src
```

finds only Gemini's own `"trust": true` setting. The signal layer the section protects was retired in #449. A reader following the security policy is told about a protection Contexere does not have.

Fix: remove section 1 and its row in the summary table, or replace it with what does guard a repository today, if anything.

inboundFeedback.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
inboundFeedback.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.
